extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Renaissance satire; students and readers of Rabelais (Gargantua)
extracted.subtask_description: A translated excerpt from Rabelais's Gargantua describing the rules, architecture, inscriptions, apparel, and lifestyle of the fictional Abbey of Theleme; aimed at readers of satirical Renaissance literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: No clocks or dials; hours by discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: In this new structure there should be neither clock nor dial, but that according to the opportunities and incident occasions all their hours should be disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gargantua: 'the greatest loss of time that I know is to count the hours. What good comes of it? ... there can be no greater dotage in the world than for one to guide and direct his courses by the sound of a bell, and not by his own judgment and discretion.' This prescribes self-regulation of daily schedule rather than fixed canonical hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission: appearance and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Into this religious order should be admitted no women that were not fair, well-featured, and of a sweet disposition; nor men that were not comely, personable, and well conditioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as corrective to contemporary convent practice (which admitted the deformed or foolish), this is a normative selection criterion based on personal beauty, comportment, and pleasant disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender composition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In this house there shall be no women in case there be not men, nor men in case there be not women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule ensuring mixed-sex presence — the abbey's admissions are contingent on presence of the opposite sex to avoid solitary single-sex membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to depart freely
rubrics_metrics.description: All whatever, men or women, admitted within this abbey, should have full leave to depart with peace and contentment whensoever it should seem good to them so to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with perpetual vows of medieval orders; this is an explicit procedural right allowing voluntary exit at will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted to marry, be rich, and live at liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: It was therefore constituted and appointed that in this convent they might be honourably married, that they might be rich, and live at liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that traditional monastic vows (chastity, poverty, obedience) are inverted: inhabitants may marry and hold wealth and freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits for admission
rubrics_metrics.description: The women were to be admitted from ten till fifteen, and the men from twelve till eighteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the legitimate ages for initiation into the order (explicit numerical bounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbey architecture and furnishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The architecture was hexagonal with six great round towers (Arctic, Calaer, Anatole, Mesembrine, Hesperia, Criere), six storeys high, 9,332 chambers each with withdrawing-room, closet, wardrobe, oratory and passage; galleries, winding staircases, libraries arranged by language, richly furnished halls, tapestries, looking-glasses, and elaborate pavements and roofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed prescriptive description of the abbey's scale, materials (porphyry, Numidian stone, serpentine marble), decorative program, and library arrangement — sets normative expectations for the building's grandeur and internal organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gate inscription — excluded classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The great gate inscription lists exclusions: 'Here enter not vile bigots, hypocrites, Externally devoted apes, ... Cursed snakes, dissembled varlets, seeming sancts, ... Here enter not attorneys, barristers, Nor bridle-champing law-practitioners: Clerks, commissaries, scribes, nor pharisees, ... Lawsuits, debates, and wrangling Hence are exiled, and jangling. ... Here enter not base pinching usurers, Pelf-lickers, everlasting gatherers, Gold-graspers, ... mangy, pocky folks shall have no place, No ugly lusks, nor persons of disgrace.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inscription serves as an explicit behavioral/professional exclusion list — banning legalists, litigious persons, usurers, hypocrites, drunkards, liars, thieves, envious, cruel, and other vices. The text uses vivid, often comic invective as both policy statement and satirical lampoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gate inscription — welcomed classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The gate also welcomes: 'All noble sparks, endowed with gallant parts... Blades of heroic breasts... pure, honest, faithful, true Expounders of the Scriptures... all ladies of high birth, Delicious, stately, charming, ...' — a list of virtues and desirable personae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive admissions policy: the abbey explicitly invites genteel, witty, courteous, scholarly, virtuous, and merry people; the welcome is rendered in celebratory verse describing attributes and rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing maxim: 'Do What Thou Wilt'
rubrics_metrics.description: The one clause to be observed in their rule: 'Do What Thou Wilt;' because men that are free, well-born, well-bred, and conversant in honest companies, have naturally an instinct and spur that prompteth them unto virtuous actions, and withdraws them from vice, which is called honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents a single libertarian governing principle with philosophical justification (liberty produces emulation towards virtue), forming the ideological core of the order's governance and behavioral rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational and skill expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members were taught so that there was neither he nor she but could read, write, sing, play several musical instruments, speak five or six languages, and compose in them all in verse and prose; valiant knights, dexterous both on foot and horseback; ladies adept at needlework and other honest actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets normative standards for the cultural, linguistic, artistic, martial, and domestic skills expected of inhabitants — an encyclopedic ideal of broad erudition and accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily attire and wardrobe practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Ladies were apparelled after their pleasure (stockings of scarlet or purple, embroidered garters, taffety farthingales, gowns of cloth of gold or satin, furs in winter, jewels, plumes). Men were apparelled in matching liveries; certain gentlemen told the youths each morning what vestments the ladies would wear; masters of the wardrobes had all raiments ready each morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative rules and practices about dress: elaborated clothing codes, matching livery between sexes, daily coordination led by the ladies' preferences, and an organized wardrobe staff and nearby craft quarter supplying garments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amenities and recreation facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The abbey grounds contain tiltyard, barriers for tournaments, hippodrome, theatre, natatory (swimming place), three-stage baths with myrtle-water, garden of pleasure with a labyrinth, courts for tennis and balloon, orchard, great park abounding with venison, shooting butts and marks, stables, and falconry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the recreational, sporting, theatrical, and pleasure facilities regarded as essential to the abbey's life and to cultivate leisure, skill, and sociability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal grooming and perfumery
rubrics_metrics.description: At the going out of the halls belonging to the ladies’ lodgings were the perfumers and trimmers; those artificers furnished the ladies’ chambers each morning with the spirit of roses, orange-flower-water, and angelica, and gave each a little precious casket vapouring choicest aromatics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative provision for daily grooming and scenting rituals — an institutionalized practice supporting refinement and luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaving practice / marriage upon departure
rubrics_metrics.description: When any man of the said abbey had a mind to go out of it, he carried along with him one of the ladies, namely, her whom he had before that chosen for his mistress, and (they) were married together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the social procedure for exit: departure commonly led to marriage with a previously chosen partner from the abbey, and continuation of devotion and amity in marriage is expected.
